note: One plain sentence per test saying what it is for, shown to the model that reads a spoken order beside the item name (server/orders/llm_fallback.py). Written by an AI assistant from the investigation definitions and the standard clinical use of each test (NICE and Royal College guidance for pre-operative testing); not reviewed by a clinician. The model only chooses among the items; nothing here decides an order.

tests.fbc: counts the blood cells: anaemia, infection, platelets
tests.crp: marker of inflammation or infection in the blood
tests.u_and_e: kidney function and the salts sodium and potassium
tests.hba1c: average blood sugar control over the last three months
tests.clotting: how well the blood clots, for bleeding risk
tests.group_and_save: blood group and antibody screen so blood can be matched and kept ready in case of a transfusion
tests.lactate_cultures: lactate and blood cultures when sepsis is suspected
tests.tryptase: marker that a severe allergic reaction has happened
tests.pregnancy: tells whether the patient is pregnant
tests.urine_dipstick: quick urine test for infection, blood, protein and sugar
tests.ecg: tracing of the electrical activity of the heart: rhythm, rate, potassium effects
tests.bmi: body mass index from height and weight: how heavy the patient is
tests.stopbang: screening questionnaire for obstructive sleep apnoea
tests.ultrasound: scan with a probe, used for the abdomen, gallbladder, liver and kidneys
tests.ct: cross-sectional X-ray scan, for example of the abdomen
tests.mrcp: magnetic resonance scan of the bile and pancreatic ducts
tests.chest_xray: plain X-ray film of the chest
tests.blood_gas: arterial blood gas: oxygen, carbon dioxide, acid balance, lactate

staff.surgeon: the operating surgeon or the surgical registrar who will operate
staff.anaesthetist: the anaesthetist, who looks after the anaesthetic and the airway
staff.senior: the senior doctor on call, to supervise or to be told of a problem or a decision
staff.nurse: a ward or theatre nurse at the bedside
staff.porter: the porter who moves the patient between departments

medicine.TR-SEPSIS-BUNDLE: the sepsis six treatment bundle to start: oxygen, fluids, antibiotics and the rest
medicine.TR-ABX-PROPHYLAXIS: one dose of antibiotic given before the skin incision to prevent a wound infection
medicine.TR-ABX-S2: antibiotics to treat an infection or sepsis that is already present
medicine.TR-FAST-SUGAR: fast sugar by mouth (glucose gel or a sugary drink) for a patient who is hypoglycaemic and awake
medicine.TR-IV-GLUCOSE: dextrose into the vein for a hypoglycaemic patient who is drowsy or cannot swallow
medicine.TR-NSAID: non-steroidal anti-inflammatory painkiller such as ibuprofen or diclofenac
medicine.TR-PARACETAMOL: paracetamol, a simple painkiller and fever reducer, given into the vein or by mouth
medicine.TR-OPIOID: strong opioid painkiller such as morphine
medicine.TR-ANTIEMETIC: anti-sickness drug such as ondansetron or cyclizine
medicine.TR-HYPERKALAEMIA: treatment of a high potassium: calcium, insulin with dextrose
medicine.TR-STEROID-COVER: hydrocortisone stress dose for a patient on long-term steroids
medicine.TR-VTE-PROPHYLAXIS: injection that prevents blood clots in the legs and lungs
medicine.TR-ADRENALINE: adrenaline for anaphylaxis or cardiac arrest
medicine.TR-OXYGEN: oxygen by mask or nasal cannula
medicine.TR-IV-FLUIDS: intravenous fluid such as saline or Hartmann's
